blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Pedogenesis is the complex process of soil profile development influenced by weathering, organic matter accumulation, and leaching.
Hans Jenny defined soil formation as a function of five factors: Climate, Organisms, Relief, Parent Material, and Time: S = f(Cl, O, R, P, T).
Climate and living organisms are active factors of soil formation, while parent rock, topography, and time are passive factors.
Eluviation refers to the washing out of minerals from the A horizon, whereas illuviation is the accumulation of these minerals in the B horizon.
Laterization occurs in humid tropical zones resulting in silica leaching and concentration of iron and aluminum oxides.

blocks.content: Soil formation is a dynamic process where rock materials are transformed under the influence of climate, organisms, topography, and time.

rows: Movement and washing out of soil dissolved or suspended materials
Deposition and accumulation of washed-out minerals from above
Horizon A and Horizon E (Exit horizon)
Clay, silicate minerals, iron, aluminum, and soluble organic compounds
Accumulated iron oxides, aluminum, silicate clays, and carbonates

items: Questions frequently ask to differentiate between Active Factors (Climate, Biosphere) and Passive Factors (Parent material, Relief, Time).
Remember the distinct soil horizons: 'E' is the horizon of maximum Eluviation, and 'B' is the horizon of Illuviation.
Podzolization occurs in cold, humid climates, whereas Laterization is characteristic of hot, wet tropical regions.
